newsitem.title: CHINA: China curbs new Sino-foreign supermarket chains.
newsitem.headline: China curbs new Sino-foreign supermarket chains.

text.p: China will not approve new Sino-foreign supermarket chains in the near future until after the promulgation of regulations governing the setting up of such ventures, the overseas edition of the People's Daily said on Monday.
"In the short term, it is difficult for Sino-foreign supermarket chains to provide experience that could be borrowed," the newspaper quoted an official of the Ministry of Internal Trade as saying.
"Hence, the government will not approve more Sino-foreign supermarket chains at this juncture," he was quoted as saying.

The ministry is drafting regulations that would allow new Sino-foreign supermarket chains in central and western China in the long term as part of Beijing's efforts to join the World Trade Organisation, the official said.
The State Council, or cabinet, approved earlier this year the setting up of Sino-Dutch and Sino-Japanese supermarket chains on a trial basis, the newspaper said.
